card.title: Benzene — substitution, not addition, preserves the ring

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Benzene's 6 π electrons satisfy Hückel (4n+2, planar ring) — delocalised, extra-stable, and hostile to addition (which would destroy aromaticity). So benzene SUBSTITUTES electrophilically instead: nitration, sulphonation, halogenation, Friedel–Crafts alkylation/acylation. Existing groups direct the next entry — activators ortho/para, deactivators meta. Prepared by decarboxylating sodium benzoate (soda lime), reducing phenol (Zn dust), or trimerising ethyne.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Hückel: planar ring + (4n+2) π e⁻ (benzene n = 1)  ·  nitration: C₆H₆ + HNO₃/H₂SO₄ → C₆H₅NO₂ (nitronium NO₂⁺)  ·  sulphonation: + fuming H₂SO₄ → C₆H₅SO₃H  ·  chlorination/FeCl₃ → C₆H₅Cl  ·  F–C alkylation: + RCl/AlCl₃ → C₆H₅R

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Electrophilic substitution needs a generated electrophile (NO₂⁺ from mixed acid, Br⁺ via FeBr₃, R⁺ via AlCl₃) — benzene ignores plain Br₂ water (unlike alkenes: the key distinction test). Hückel demands planarity + conjugation; non-planar 4n+2 rings stay non-aromatic. Free combustion only (sooty flame from high C%).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Phenol's −OH activates so fiercely that bromination needs no catalyst (white 2,4,6-tribromophenol). −NO₂/−COOH/−SO₃H deactivate to meta. Friedel–Crafts alkylation rearranges carbocations and over-alkylates; acylation then Clemmensen fixes both. Cyclooctatetraene (8 π, tub-shaped) fails Hückel by geometry.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Benzene + conc. HNO₃/conc. H₂SO₄ → nitrobenzene (NO₂⁺ attacks, H⁺ leaves, aromaticity intact); + fuming H₂SO₄ → benzenesulphonic acid; + Cl₂/FeCl₃ → chlorobenzene (NEB 2022, 3 marks — three equations, three electrophiles, one mechanism pattern: generate E⁺, substitute, restore the ring).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Hückel is necessary, not sufficient (strain and heteroatom effects intrude). Orientation rules guide but mixtures still form (o/p split). Forcing addition needs extremes (Ni/H₂ heat → cyclohexane; Cl₂/UV → 666/gammexane) — proof of aromatic resistance, not everyday chemistry.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Mechanism template: E⁺ adds to the ring forming the arenium (σ-complex) ion — positive charge delocalised over three carbons (draw all three resonance forms) — then base removes the ring H⁺, restoring aromaticity. The slow step keeps the ring intact; addition would pay the ~150 kJ/mol resonance penalty, so substitution wins kinetically.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Director cheat: activators (OH, NH₂, alkyl) → o/p; deactivators (NO₂, COOH, SO₃H) → meta; halogens → o/p but deactivating (the exception). 'Benzene + Br₂ water' → NO reaction (vs alkenes decolourise) — the classic distinction question.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2022 (3): benzene + mixed acid / fuming H₂SO₄ / Cl₂-FeCl₃ reactions. NEB 2021 (3): resonance in benzene — contributing structures + two consequences. Prep routes and orientation rules rotate yearly.
